scenes.tts: Photoreceptors release one transmitter, glutamate. More in the dark, less in the light. Yet some bipolar cells depolarize to light, and others hyperpolarize. How?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Transmitter, Two Signs. A cone terminal releases many glutamate dots in the dark, few in the light. Two bipolar cells below it: one voltage trace goes up, the other down. Question on screen: one transmitter, two signs?
scenes.narration: Photoreceptors release one transmitter, glutamate. More in the dark, less in the light. Yet some bipolar cells depolarize to light, and others hyperpolarize. How?

scenes.tts: Picture one cone terminal feeding two bipolar cells. On the left, darkness. On the right, light.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left half dark, right half lit. In each half, one cone terminal contacts two bipolar cells, labelled OFF and ON.
scenes.narration: Picture one cone terminal feeding two bipolar cells. On the left, darkness. On the right, light.

scenes.tts: The off bipolar cell has ionotropic glutamate receptors. Glutamate opens their cation channels, so in the dark the cell is depolarized.
scenes.caption: The OFF bipolar cell has ionotropic glutamate receptors. Glutamate opens their cation channels, so in the dark the cell is depolarized.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the OFF cell, dark side: glutamate binds receptors that open cation channels; ions flow in; its voltage trace sits high. Label: AMPA or kainate receptors.
scenes.narration: The OFF bipolar cell has ionotropic glutamate receptors. Glutamate opens their cation channels, so in the dark the cell is depolarized.

scenes.tts: Light lowers glutamate, so the excitation fades, and the cell hyperpolarizes. The sign is kept.
scenes.visual: Light side: fewer glutamate dots, channels close, the OFF trace falls. A sign-ledger strip appears along the bottom. Label: sign kept.
scenes.narration: Light lowers glutamate, so the excitation fades, and the cell hyperpolarizes. The sign is kept.

scenes.tts: The on bipolar cell uses a different receptor, a metabotropic one. In the dark, glutamate on this receptor activates a G protein.
scenes.caption: The ON bipolar cell uses a different receptor, a metabotropic one. In the dark, glutamate on this receptor activates a G protein.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the ON cell, dark side: glutamate binds a receptor that switches on a G protein. Labels: mGluR6; Go.
scenes.narration: The ON bipolar cell uses a different receptor, a metabotropic one. In the dark, glutamate on this receptor activates a G protein.

scenes.tts: That G protein holds a cation channel shut. So in the dark, the on cell is hyperpolarized.
scenes.caption: That G protein holds a cation channel shut. So in the dark, the ON cell is hyperpolarized.
scenes.visual: The active G protein clamps a channel closed, drawn as a brake. The ON trace sits low. Label: TRPM1, held shut.
scenes.narration: That G protein holds a cation channel shut. So in the dark, the ON cell is hyperpolarized.

scenes.tts: Light lowers glutamate. The G protein's activity falls, the brake comes off, and the channel opens. The cell depolarizes. The sign is inverted.
scenes.visual: Light side: fewer glutamate dots, the G protein goes quiet, the brake lifts, TRPM1 opens, ions flow in, the ON trace rises. Label: sign inverted.
scenes.narration: Light lowers glutamate. The G protein's activity falls, the brake comes off, and the channel opens. The cell depolarizes. The sign is inverted.

scenes.tts: Keep a ledger of the flips. The photoreceptor flips the sign once. The off cell adds no flip. The on cell adds a second.
scenes.caption: Keep a ledger of the flips. The photoreceptor flips the sign once. The OFF cell adds no flip. The ON cell adds a second.
scenes.visual: The ledger fills: photons more (+); cone voltage down (−); glutamate down (−); OFF bipolar (−); ON bipolar (+). Each flip marked with a curved arrow.
scenes.narration: Keep a ledger of the flips. The photoreceptor flips the sign once. The OFF cell adds no flip. The ON cell adds a second.

scenes.tts: An even number of flips means the cell responds like light. That makes it an on cell.
scenes.caption: An even number of flips means the cell responds like light. That makes it an ON cell.
scenes.visual: The ON row's two flips highlighted. Rule of thumb on screen: even number of inversions = ON.
scenes.narration: An even number of flips means the cell responds like light. That makes it an ON cell.

scenes.tts: How do we know the receptors differ? Slaughter and Miller recorded inside cells of the mudpuppy retina.
scenes.visual: A mudpuppy, a salamander, then its retina kept as a perfused eyecup with a fine electrode in one cell. Label: Slaughter and Miller, 1981.
scenes.narration: How do we know the receptors differ? Slaughter and Miller recorded inside cells of the mudpuppy retina.

scenes.tts: They bathed the retina in a glutamate mimic that acts on the on receptor.
scenes.caption: They bathed the retina in a glutamate mimic that acts on the ON receptor.
scenes.visual: Solution flows over the eyecup. Label: APB, a glutamate analogue acting at the ON receptor.
scenes.narration: They bathed the retina in a glutamate mimic that acts on the ON receptor.

scenes.tts: Add the drug, then turn on a light. What does the on cell do? And the off cell?
scenes.caption: Add the drug, then turn on a light. What does the ON cell do? And the OFF cell?
scenes.visual: Two stylized intracellular records, ON and OFF, each with a light-step bar beneath. Drug bar on. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Add the drug, then turn on a light. What does the ON cell do? And the OFF cell?

scenes.tts: The on responses vanished. The drug held the on cells in their dark state, so light had nothing to remove.
scenes.caption: The ON responses vanished. The drug held the ON cells in their dark state, so light had nothing to remove.
scenes.visual: The ON record stays flat at its dark level during the light step. Label: ON response abolished.
scenes.narration: The ON responses vanished. The drug held the ON cells in their dark state, so light had nothing to remove.

scenes.tts: The off responses carried on, in the same retina. So the two cells read glutamate with different receptors.
scenes.caption: The OFF responses carried on, in the same retina. So the two cells read glutamate with different receptors.
scenes.visual: The OFF record still steps down with light. Label: OFF response spared (control in the same retina).
scenes.narration: The OFF responses carried on, in the same retina. So the two cells read glutamate with different receptors.

scenes.tts: Each cone feeds two streams, one for lighter, one for darker. The takeaway: the receptor, not the molecule, sets the sign.
scenes.visual: The cone splits into two lines running down to ON and OFF ganglion cells, labelled lighter and darker. Takeaway on screen: the receptor, not the molecule, sets the sign.
scenes.narration: Each cone feeds two streams, one for lighter, one for darker. The takeaway: the receptor, not the molecule, sets the sign.
